title: India's Best-Selling SUVs Are Going Hybrid: Creta, Seltos, and Duster to Get Electrified Powertrains
excerpt: Hyundai, Kia, and Renault are preparing hybrid versions of their top-selling SUVs for the Indian market by 2027, challenging Toyota and Maruti Suzuki's grip on the segment.
body:
• Three of India's best-selling SUVs — the Renault Duster, Kia Seltos, and Hyundai Creta — are set to receive hybrid powertrains by 2027.
  • Renault's Duster Hybrid arrives first, likely in Q4 2026, with a 156 hp system that promises 1,000 km range on a full tank and up to 40% reduction in fuel consumption.
  • Kia confirmed hybrid variants for the Seltos, Carens, and Sonet at its April 2026 CEO Investor Day, with the Seltos Hybrid expected first in early 2027.
  • Hyundai's next-generation Creta will launch in 2027 with a hybrid option, alongside two new 7-seater hybrid SUVs, directly challenging Toyota and Maruti Suzuki's dominance.

India's hybrid SUV market, long dominated by Toyota and Maruti Suzuki, is about to get significantly more competitive. Hyundai, Kia, and Renault are all preparing hybrid versions of their volume-leading SUVs, with launches planned between late 2026 and 2027.

Renault Duster: First to Market

The third-generation Renault Duster, launched earlier this year, will be the first of the three to receive a hybrid powertrain. The Duster Hybrid is expected to arrive in the fourth quarter of 2026, combining an 80 kW (107 hp) 1.8-litre direct injection petrol engine with a 36 kW (48 hp) electric motor driving the front wheels through a 1.4 kWh battery pack.

Total system output is expected to reach 116 kW (156 hp) with 172 Nm of torque. Renault claims the system allows city driving in EV mode approximately 80% of the time, with up to 40% reduction in fuel consumption compared to the conventional powertrain. With a full tank, the Duster Hybrid should manage up to 1,000 kilometres without refuelling — a significant selling point for Indian consumers conscious of running costs.

Kia Seltos: Confirmed at the Top Level

At its 2026 CEO Investor Day in April, Kia confirmed hybrid powertrains for three Indian models between 2027 and 2029: the Seltos, Carens, and Sonet. The Seltos Hybrid is expected to be the first to market, potentially arriving as early as the beginning of 2027, according to industry reports from Gaadiwaadi.

Internationally, the Kia Seltos Hybrid uses a 1.6-litre petrol engine with an electric motor, but the India-specific version is likely to employ a locally manufactured 1.5-litre petrol engine with a front-mounted electric motor in a front-wheel-drive configuration. The hybrid Seltos is expected to command a premium of approximately ₹2 lakh over its conventional counterparts, according to India Car News.

Hyundai Creta: The Volume King Goes Green

The next-generation Hyundai Creta, codenamed SX3, is expected to arrive in 2027 with a comprehensive overhaul that includes India's first hybrid Creta. The current second-generation Creta crossed 2 lakh annual units in FY26 — the only mid-size SUV to achieve that milestone — meaning a hybrid option in this segment carries genuine market weight.

Spy shots from testing in Jaipur and Manali show the third-generation Creta with a boxier design, approximately 100 mm longer than the current model, and Hyundai's new Pleos Connect infotainment system. The hybrid powertrain is expected to use a modified version of Hyundai's 1.5-litre petrol engine, shared with the Kia Seltos platform.

Beyond the Creta, Hyundai is also developing two 7-seater hybrid SUVs for India: the Ni1i (codenamed), based on the long-wheelbase Tucson and expected at ₹20–25 lakh, and a potential Palisade Hybrid at the premium end.

Breaking Toyota's Monopoly

The entry of three major manufacturers into the hybrid segment represents a direct challenge to Toyota and Maruti Suzuki, whose Hyryder, Grand Vitara, and Innova HyCross currently account for roughly 80% of hybrid passenger vehicle volumes in India. With government incentives for hybrid technology and rising fuel costs driving consumer interest, the competition is likely to accelerate.

What It Means for Buyers

For Indian car buyers — including NRI families considering vehicle purchases during visits home — the expanding hybrid lineup offers more fuel-efficient options without the range anxiety of pure EVs. With three proven nameplates going hybrid, the technology is moving from niche to mainstream in India's largest SUV segments.
